div.head: CHn cor Prol.
div.ab: [Für Worcestershire] Henricus rex Anglorum Samsoni episcopo et Ursoni de Abetot et omnibus baronibus et fidelibus suis tam Francigenis quam Angligenis de Wirecestrescira salutem.
[Für Hertfordshire] Henricus Dei gratia rex Angl[orum] Hugoni de Boclande uicecomiti et omnibus fidelibus suis tam Francis quam Anglis in Her[t]fordscire salutem.
[Archiv zu Winchester?] Henricus Dei gratia rex Anglorum omnibus baronibus et fidelibus suis tam Francigenis quam Anglis salutem.
Anno incarnationis Dominicae MCI, Henricus, filius Willelmi regis, post obitum fratris sui Willelmi Dei gratia rex Anglorum, omnibus [baronibus et] fidelibus suis tam Francigenis quam Anglis salutem.

In the year of the incarnation of our Lord 1101, Henry, son of King William, after the death of his brother William, by the grace of God King of England, to all his barons and loyal subjects both French and English—greeting.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 276–277 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 521, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: Keines der Originale ist vorhanden, der Text aber aus Chronisten und Urkundensammlungen des 12./13. Jhs. sicher herstellbar, ausgenommen Zweifelhaftes in stilistischen Kleinigkeiten, worin vielleicht schon die Originale variirten. Ich setze statt ae, ę und das e gleicher Bedeutung hier æ. Die Varianten stehen vollständiger in Transact. R. Histor. soc. N. S. VIII p. 40; hier bleiben fort alle, die sicher Schreiber-Irrthümer sind. Unter den folgenden Varianten tragen * diejenigen, welche mehreren Classen der Hss. eigen, also wohl sicher zurückgehen auf Verschiedenheit schon zwischen den Originalen; mit † bezeichne ich Varianten Einer Classe, die nur vielleicht in Einem Originale standen.

None of the originals survives, but the text can be securely restored from chroniclers and cartularies of the 12th/13th cent., except for doubtful points in stylistic details, in which the originals themselves perhaps already varied. Here I substitute æ for ae, ę and e of the same value. The variants are given more fully in Transact. R. Histor. soc. N. S. VIII p. 40; all those that are certainly scribal errors are omitted here. Among the following variants, those that are common to several classes of the MSS, and so almost certainly go back to differences already between the originals, bear *; with † I mark variants of a single class, which only perhaps stood in a single original.

Dass nicht etwa Herefordshire, wie die Hs. vermuten liesse, gemeint sei, beweist der Name des Sheriffs. Da die Verwechslung mit Hertfordshire häufig vorkam, hiess jenes oft in Wallia. Urkunden Heinrichs I. für St. Albans an Buckland adressiert oder von ihm bezeugt stehen in Matth. Paris ed. Luard VI 37—40; Ordric XI nennt ihn unter Heinrichs I. Günstlingen niederer Abkunft; er diente schon Wilhelm II.; Davis Reg. Agnorm. Index; vgl. o. II 327: Bocland; Round Geoffrey 309. 328. 355; Rymer Foed. I 10. 12; vicecomiti de Herefordsyra Liber Eli. p. 298

That it is not, say, Herefordshire that is meant, as the MS might suggest, is proved by the name of the sheriff. Since confusion with Hertfordshire was frequent, the former was often called in Wallia. Charters of Henry I for St. Albans addressed to Buckland or witnessed by him are in Matth. Paris ed. Luard VI 37—40; Ordric XI names him among Henry I’s favourites of low birth; he had already served William II; Davis Reg. Agnorm. Index; cf. above II 327: Bocland; Round Geoffrey 309. 328. 355; Rymer Foed. I 10. 12; vicecomiti de Herefordsyra Liber Eli. p. 298
S. o. Einl. n. 1. Es fällt auf, dass Prälaten und Grafen vor den baronibus fehlen. Wie Q unten in Hn com die besondere Adresse verstümmelte, so vielleicht ein anderer Schreiber hier
See above Introduction n. 1. It is striking that prelates and earls are missing before the baronibus. Just as Q below in Hn com mutilated the particular address, so perhaps did another scribe here

Die Worte ‘von Gottes Gnaden’ können entweder einigen echten Exemplaren gehören [vgl. Birch Jl. Brit. archl. ass. 29, 236; Rymer Foed. I 9; o. S. 273 Z. 5] oder (wie von Q zu Hn com Pro{b}) nachträglich späterem Brauche gemäss interpoliert sein. Dagegen liess sie schwerlich irgendein Schreiber willkürlich fort. Im ganzen ist Dei gratia damals seltener; Hardy Rot. chart. I p. xv. Heinrich nennt sich König nutu Dei im Briefe jener Tage an Anselm

The words ‘by the grace of God’ may either belong to some genuine copies [cf. Birch Jl. Brit. archl. ass. 29, 236; Rymer Foed. I 9; above p. 273 l. 5] or (as by Q in Hn com Pro{b}) have been interpolated afterwards in accordance with later usage. On the other hand, it is hardly likely that any scribe omitted them arbitrarily. On the whole, Dei gratia is rarer at that time; Hardy Rot. chart. I p. xv. Henry calls himself king nutu Dei in his letter to Anselm of those days
Samson war Bischof, Abetot Sheriff von Worcester; Flor. Wig. 1074; Will. Malm. Pont. 116 Ende; Round Feudal Engl. 309. 313. 423; Davis Reg. Agnorm., Index
Samson was bishop, and Abetot sheriff, of Worcester; Flor. Wig. 1074; Will. Malm. Pont. 116 end; Round Feudal Engl. 309. 313. 423; Davis Reg. Agnorm., Index
Neben den Kronlehnsträgern steht der weitere Begriff fideles, ‘Untertanen’ ohne lehnrechtlichen Sondersinn, auch Wl ep Pro{b} o. S. 275
Alongside the tenants-in-chief stands the wider concept fideles, ‘subjects’, without any special feudal sense, as also in Wl ep Pro{b} above p. 275
